title: Guidelines for Using the Welcome Banner

chapters.title: Banner design principles and checklist functionality
Checklist structure and user navigation freedom
Building user confidence and content variety
Best practices for checklist scale and conclusion

features.name: Welcome banner
features.description: A banner that greets users when they arrive at the role center in Business Central, serving as an entrance point for onboarding and getting started.

features.name: User checklist
features.description: The main onboarding piece that appears after clicking an action in the banner, providing overview and structure of relevant activities to guide users through discovering key values in Business Central.
caveats: users can move and navigate freely between tasks and may skip some tasks to revisit later

features.name: Evaluation and trial checklist
features.description: A type of checklist designed for trial situations where the goal is to help users experience value propositions. Should be kept short and with minimal friction to accommodate customer time constraints.

features.name: Go-live checklist
features.description: A checklist designed for go-live situations focused on setting up Business Central and users for actual work, with more involved items related to permissions and user setup configured in a role-oriented manner.
caveats: setup should be kept as short as possible

features.name: Assisted setup
features.description: An alternative to checklists for handling additional setup items when the number of checklist items exceeds recommended limits, allowing guidance to users through an assisted setup list.
caveats: should be used when checklist items exceed five to seven items
